Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:

        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Preserve speculative binder when checking local Main signatures
Issues.Body:
Speculative binding of a top-level local function named `Main` returning `Task` or `Task<T>` throws `KeyNotFoundException` because entry-point signature checking requests a compilation binder for speculative syntax.

**Implementation is pending plan approval; no code changes have been made.**

- **Proposed fix:** Thread an optional binder through `HasEntryPointSignature` and `ReturnsAwaitableToVoidOrInt`, supplying the local function’s binder.
- **Proposed regression coverage:** Exercise speculative return-type binding for async and non-async functions under executable and library output.

- Fixes #86103

Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3658

Reloading an .lscache currently restores every C# analyzer from a referenced framework pack, including analyzers MSBuild removed. This can cause duplicate logging generators and enable off-by-default generators in the editor even when command-line builds are clean.

Preserve MSBuild’s actual analyzer selection while keeping caches compact and environment-independent:

- Add frameworkAnalyzerReferences for selected targeting-pack analyzers. 
- Replace sdkAnalyzerPacks with sdkAnalyzerPackageReferences for selected analyzers from SDK-known NuGet packages. 
- Store compressed, pack-relative paths without installation roots or package versions, and load only the recorded files. 
- Keep selections in their target-framework slices so common entries cannot bind to the wrong pack version. 
- Leave metadata-reference pack expansion unchanged. 
- Bump the cache format to version 3 so older readers cannot silently misinterpret the new selection semantics. Version 2 caches require regeneration.

Issues.Title: Fix Razor rename issue with using aliases
Issues.Body:
Found while working on adding proper support for using aliases to Razor, and thought it was worth splitting out to a separate PR.

Sonic gave us two generated C# documents per Razor document, a "decl" and "impl" document, and each one gets all of the using directives emitted to it. Using aliases in C# are document local, however, so when renaming one, Roslyn only (correctly) renamed things in one of the two documents. This meant that there would be compile errors in the result, either from one document still using the old alias, or from the using directive edit being dropped because it was assumed that edits to using directives would be equivalent in both documents.

The solution, and what this PR does, is twofold: 1, detect a rename of an alias, and collect rename edits from both documents, and 2, combine and map edits from both documents to Razor _before_ processing using directives.

Issues.Title: FBA: Fix unreliable DTBs of `#:ref` target projects
Issues.Body:
Fixes an issue reported on Teams by @DamianEdwards

This might have been a regression introduced by #84139, though I need to double check.

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/65d349930a64a00fb6588bd0dc17e41f05993781/src/Workspaces/MSBuild/BuildHost/Build/ProjectBuildManager.cs#L226
 
It looks like because we are not creating an intermediate `MSB.Evaluation.Project`, but instead going straight to `ProjectInstance`, the full `projectRootElement` does not get explicitly retained in the `_projectCollection`.
 
Then here: https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/blob/4f3669e6c4d4f1aaaf2bd52eed8337a2c0f9fe52/src/Build/Evaluation/ProjectRootElementCache.cs#L290

I believe what is happening is: msbuild might need the `projectRootElement` holding the referent project of the `#:ref` later, in order to load it. But depending on whether it was in cache (see `_strongCache`/`_weakCache` fields), it might end up going to disk to look for it. It's an in-memory project though, so going to disk won't work, and will result in the failure Damian observed. The failure is nondeterministic and seems more likely to occur when lots of different projects are being loaded.

I fixed this by explicitly creating an `Evaluation.Project` and loading that into the `_projectCollection`. This has the effect of explicitly retaining the `projectRootElement`.

One issue here is I don't think these get unloaded. Some investigation is needed to find the appropriate point at which to unload, I believe it is not the Dispose method of the containing type where the impl change was made.

But, it doesn't look like our MSBuildHost dealt with unloading at all until recently, so perhaps we can live without unloading of in-memory projects for the short term.
 
I think in the medium/long term we should talk to msbuild about our practice of building projects which don't exist on disk. We should set things up so it's easier to verify things are correct "by construction".

---

I was able to verify that the new test failed reliably before the change and passes afterwards.

I opted not to add an explicitly FBA/end-to-end test as exposing the ability to clear the cache in the remote msbuild host at the right time to repro the bug seemed excessively difficult. Instead I am just testing in MSBuildHost tests "locally".

 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86231)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "FBA: Fix unreliable DTBs of `#:ref` target projects" (#86231)

Issues.Title: VB.NET: CInt(Math.Truncate(Double)) returns 22 instead of 21 inside an Async method
Issues.Body:
# VB.NET: `CInt(Math.Truncate(Double))` returns 22 instead of 21 inside an Async method

## Description

The expression `CInt(Math.Truncate(x))` produces different results depending on whether it is executed inside a regular method or an `Async` method.

When `x` is `21.5R`, the expression should return `21`, because `Math.Truncate` returns `21.0`. However, inside an `Async` method, `CInt(Math.Truncate(x))` returns `22`.

This behavior is reproducible in a .NET 10 console application and a clean WPF application. It also occurs in my existing WPF application, BloyectDesk.

## Minimal reproduction

```vb
Imports System
Imports System.Threading.Tasks

Module Program

    Sub Main(args As String())

        Console.WriteLine("Synchronous method:")
        TestConversions()

        Console.WriteLine()
        MainAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult()

        Console.ReadKey()

    End Sub

    Sub TestConversions()

        Dim x As Double = 21.5R

        Dim a As Integer = CInt(Math.Truncate(x))
        Dim b As Integer = CInt(Math.Truncate(CDbl(x)))
        Dim c As Integer = CInt(Math.Truncate(21.5R))
        Dim d As Integer = Convert.ToInt32(Math.Truncate(x))

        Console.WriteLine($"Truncate: {Math.Truncate(x)}")
        Console.WriteLine($"a = {a}")
        Console.WriteLine($"b = {b}")
        Console.WriteLine($"c = {c}")
        Console.WriteLine($"d = {d}")

    End Sub

    Async Function MainAsync() As Task

        Console.WriteLine("Async method:")

        Dim x As Double = 21.5R

        Dim a As Integer = CInt(Math.Truncate(x))
        Dim b As Integer = CInt(Math.Truncate(CDbl(x)))
        Dim c As Integer = CInt(Math.Truncate(21.5R))
        Dim d As Integer = Convert.ToInt32(Math.Truncate(x))

        Console.WriteLine($"Truncate: {Math.Truncate(x)}")
        Console.WriteLine($"a = {a}")
        Console.WriteLine($"b = {b}")
        Console.WriteLine($"c = {c}")
        Console.WriteLine($"d = {d}")

        Await Task.CompletedTask

    End Function

End Module
```

## Actual behavior

Synchronous method:

```text
Truncate: 21
a = 21
b = 21
c = 21
d = 21
```

Async method:

```text
Truncate: 21
a = 22
b = 22
c = 22
d = 21
```

## Expected behavior

Both methods should produce the same results:

```text
Truncate: 21
a = 21
b = 21
c = 21
d = 21
```

`Math.Truncate(21.5R)` returns `21.0`. Converting that value to `Integer` should produce `21`, regardless of whether the expression is inside an asynchronous method.

## Additional observations

- The behavior reproduces in a .NET 10 console application.
- It also reproduces in a clean WPF application targeting .NET 10 for Windows.
- The same expressions behave correctly in a synchronous method.
- `Convert.ToInt32(Math.Truncate(x))` consistently returns `21`.
- The issue appears to be associated with the VB.NET compiler's handling of `CInt(Math.Truncate(...))` inside an `Async` method.

I have not yet confirmed whether this is related to a particular compiler version or optimization setting.

## Environment

- Target framework: .NET 10
- Language: Visual Basic .NET
- Operating system: Windows
- IDE: Visual Studio (exact version to be provided)
- VB compiler version: To be confirmed

Could this be a compiler bug in the handling or optimization of `CInt(Math.Truncate(...))` inside asynchronous methods?

Issues.Title: Limit the CA1704 numeric name exemption to type parameters
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #85162, addressing https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/85162#discussion_r4383832691.

### Problem

#85162 exempted single-digit names from the "unmeaningful name" check so that `T1`, `T2`, … are no longer reported. Its description assumed only type parameters (`T` prefix) and interfaces (`I` prefix) could produce a bare digit after prefix stripping. Fields have their `_` prefix stripped too, so the exemption also let these through:

```csharp
class C
{
    int _1;          // no longer reported
}
interface I1 { }     // no longer reported
```

`_1` and `I1` are no more meaningful than `_c` or `ID`, which are still reported.

### Fix

The digit exemption now applies only to `SymbolKind.TypeParameter`, where `T1` is the BCL convention (`Func<T1, T2>`, `HashCode.Combine<T1, …>`):

```csharp
if (checkForUnmeaningful && symbolName.Length == 1 && !(symbol.Kind == SymbolKind.TypeParameter && IsWordNumeric(symbolName)))
```

### Tests

- `_1` added to `UnmeaningfulMembers` (field, reported)
- `I1` added to `TypeUnmeaningful_Verify_EmitsDiagnosticAsync` (interface, reported)
- The `T1`/`T2`/`T10` tests from #85162 still pass unchanged

All 76 CA1704 tests in Text.Analyzers.UnitTests pass.

### Notes for review

- This restores the behavior from before #85162 for fields and interfaces. Type parameters keep the fix.
- No rule added, removed or re-leveled, so no AnalyzerReleases entry.

Issues.Title: Hot reload crashes with "An item with the same key has already been added. Key: 0" editing an async method with captures and an await in catch/finally
Issues.Body:
## Description

Editing a method under `dotnet watch` crashes the watcher with an `ArgumentException` from
`DefinitionMap.MakeLambdaAndClosureMapFromMetadata` when the method:

1. is `async`,
2. has lambdas that capture **both** a parameter and a local declared in the method body, and
3. contains an `await` inside a `catch` or `finally` block.

Removing any one of the three makes the problem go away.

The baseline PDB already has the bad data. The method's `EncLambdaAndClosureMap` custom debug
information (`A643004C-0240-496F-A783-30D64F4979DE`) holds **two closures with syntax offset 0**:
the parameter closure and the body-scope closure, which become separate scopes once the
await-in-catch/finally rewrite runs. `MakeLambdaAndClosureMapFromMetadata` builds a dictionary keyed
on `SyntaxOffset` via `ToImmutableSegmentedDictionary`, so it throws on the duplicate.

`dotnet watch` then exits, killing the app, instead of falling back to a restart.

## Repro

`Repro1.csproj`
```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup><OutputType>Exe</OutputType><TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework><ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings></PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

`Program.cs`
```csharp
while (true) { await C.P1(1); await Task.Delay(1000); }
static class C
{
    static Task<bool> F(Func<int, bool> f) => Task.FromResult(f(1));
    public static async Task P1(int p)
    {
        await F(x => x == p);   // lambda captures a parameter
        var l = 1;
        await F(x => x == l);   // lambda captures a local
        Console.WriteLine("v1");
        try { await Task.Yield(); } catch (Exception) { await Task.Yield(); }   // await in catch (finally behaves the same)
    }
}
```

1. `dotnet watch run`
2. Change `"v1"` to `"v2"` and save.

### Expected
The change is applied, or `dotnet watch` reports a rude edit and restarts.

### Actual
```
dotnet watch ❌ An unexpected error occurred: System.ArgumentException: An item with the same key has already been added. Key: 0
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Collections.Internal.ThrowHelper.ThrowAddingDuplicateWithKeyArgumentException[T](T key)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Collections.SegmentedDictionary`2.TryInsert(TKey key, TValue value, InsertionBehavior behavior)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Collections.ImmutableSegmentedDictionary`2.ValueBuilder.AddRange(IEnumerable`1 items)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Collections.ImmutableSegmentedDictionary`2.AddRange(IEnumerable`1 pairs)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Collections.ImmutableSegmentedDictionary.ToImmutableSegmentedDictionary[TSource,TKey,TValue](...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Emit.DefinitionMap.MakeLambdaAndClosureMapFromMetadata(EditAndContinueMethodDebugInformation debugInfo, IMethodSymbolInternal method, DebugId methodId, IReadOnlyDictionary`2& lambdaMap, IReadOnlyDictionary`2& closureMap)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Emit.DefinitionMap.TryCreateVariableSlotAllocator(...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.MethodCompiler.LowerBodyOrInitializer(...)
   ...
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Emit.EmitHelpers.EmitDifference(...)
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.EditAndContinue.EditSession.EmitSolutionUpdateAsync(...)
   at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.CompilationHandler.HandleManagedCodeChangesAsync(...)
```

## Closure map variants (from the baseline PDB)

| Method shape | Closure syntax offsets |
|---|---|
| captures param + local, `await` in `catch` | `[0, 0]` ❌ |
| captures param + local, `await` in `finally` | `[0, 0]` ❌ |
| captures param + local (one lambda), `await` in `catch` | `[0, 0]` ❌ |
| captures param + local, no `await` in `catch` | `[0]` ✅ |
| captures two locals (no param), `await` in `catch` | `[0]` ✅ |
| captures param only, `await` in `catch` | `[0]` ✅ |

## Impact

This is a common shape in real code: transactional service methods that query by a parameter, capture
locals in later lambdas, and `await transaction.RollbackAsync()` in a `catch`. 23 methods in our
application's main service assembly have the duplicate, and every edit to any of them kills
`dotnet watch`.

## Environment

- Reproduced on SDK **10.0.102** and **10.0.403** (macOS arm64). The 11.0.100-rc.3 compiler emits the
  same duplicate offsets in the PDB. I didn't get its `dotnet watch` to run, so the crash itself isn't
  confirmed there.
- `dotnet watch run` (CLI)

## Related

Another user reported the same `Key: 0` stack on SDK 10.0.101 in a comment on dotnet/sdk#45455, with
no repro. That issue was about a different, already-fixed crash.

Issues.Title: Preserve existing newlines in unchanged complex trivia
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Preserve existing newline sequences in complex-trivia whitespace when the formatter would otherwise change only the newline encoding.

Tab-indented comments take the complex-trivia formatting path even when correctly formatted. That path regenerates whitespace using the configured newline, which defaults to the platform newline. On Windows this can introduce CRLF into an otherwise LF file and produce IDE0055 diagnostics without any indentation change.

The shared trivia formatter now preserves original non-elastic whitespace when its spacing and line structure already match the desired output, ignoring only EOL encoding. Both text-change and syntax-trivia outputs use this path. Genuine indentation, spacing, trailing-whitespace, and line-count changes, as well as elastic whitespace, continue to use the preferred newline.

This follows the existing ordinary-whitespace behavior: `end_of_line` controls generated or rebuilt whitespace, rather than requiring the core formatter to normalize every existing newline.

Related: dotnet/vscode-csharp#6817.

## Tests

- Added permanent C# coverage for matching and opposite LF/CRLF preferences, default options, tabs/spaces, mixed line endings, genuine corrections, inserted newlines with and without comments, and elastic whitespace.
- Added VB regression coverage for matching and opposite LF/CRLF preferences.
- Verified the newline-preservation regressions fail against the unfixed implementation and pass with the fix. Tests cover text-change and syntax-trivia output.
- C# workspace formatting tests: 730 passed, 1 existing skip.
- VB workspace formatting tests: 229 passed.
- Both affected test projects built successfully with `RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true`.
- Repository whitespace formatting verification and `git diff --check` passed.
- A 48-case probe using locally built assemblies confirmed that actual IDE0055 analysis no longer reports correctly formatted comment whitespace solely for an EOL mismatch, while genuine corrections still produce diagnostics and preferred-EOL output.

Validation ran on Windows with .NET 10. No live VS Code LSP-host or .NET Framework test run was performed. Builds reported existing package-vulnerability warnings.

Issues.Title: Add a fixall in document LSP code action
Issues.Body:
Adds support for `CodeActionParams.Context.Only` so that the server only calculates code actions for the requested kinds (Quick Fix, Refactoring, etc..). 

Also, adds support for the `source.fixAll` kind. This creates a special code action which fixes all diagnostics in the specified document. 

A `dotnet.codeAction.fixAllMinimumSeverity` option is added which filters the diagnostics to fix. The default value is set to `warning` which matches dotnet-format's default fix severity.

Issues.Title: Preserve generated document query parameters through URI serialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Construct source-generated document URIs from logical components so they survive normal vscode-uri parsing and serialization.

The generated-document query has two distinct escaping layers: parameter values are escaped first, and the complete parameter string is then assigned as the logical URI query component. Normal URI serialization escapes that component. Deserialization reads `ParsedUri.Query` to remove the URI layer before `HttpUtility.ParseQueryString` removes the parameter-value layer.

- Add a component-based `ParsedUri.From` factory using the existing normalization, validation, and encoding implementation.
- Use it to construct source-generated document URIs without prematurely decoding parameter escapes.
- Preserve regression coverage for direct and default-client roundtrips, special characters, Unicode, and optional generator assembly paths, plus factory formatting and validation.

This supports the default URI serialization change in https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/pull/9921. No legacy-client compatibility fallback is included. Clients using `toString(true)` still work for ordinary names but are not universally compatible: values containing ampersands, plus signs, or literal percent escapes can be corrupted.

## Verification

- Before the fix, all ten new-client regression cases failed with `Could not get documentId` after normal client serialization; after the fix, they pass.
- Focused tests after removing legacy-client characterization coverage: **189 passed, 1 skipped** (existing Unix-only case on Windows):
  ```
  dotnet test src\LanguageServer\ProtocolUnitTests\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.Protocol.UnitTests.csproj -f net10.0 --no-restore --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SourceGeneratedDocumentUrisTests|FullyQualifiedName~ParsedUriTests" -p:RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true --verbosity quiet
  ```
- Analyzer-enabled builds succeeded for the runnable language server and the shared Protocol project's `netstandard2.0` target. Existing dependency vulnerability warnings remain.
- Changed files formatted with `dotnet format whitespace`; `git diff --check` passes.
- End-to-end: vscode-csharp's `sourceGenerator.integration.test.ts` test **"Navigates to reference in source generated file"** passed against the locally built server through `DOTNET_ROSLYN_SERVER_PATH`, with the PR's default URI serializer (**1 passed, exit code 0**). The same test previously reproduced a timeout/server crash against the pinned Roslyn package.

 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86228)

Issues.Title: Cache aggregated tag helper diagnostics
Issues.Body:
From the dump in https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Significant-intellisense-lag-when-adding/11169845, repeated calls to get all the diagnostics from a tag helper, which are immutable and shared across documents, just allocated a bunch of arrays as different documents flattened the same set into the same list. This just caches them lazily.

There is a slight hit for small list sizes on the first call, but pretty big wins for repeated calls.

Attributes | Diagnostics | First call before | First call after | Repeated call before | Repeated call after
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
0 | 0 | 27.7 | 41.2 | 18.5 | 11.7
0 | 1 | 30.3 | 74.5 | 25.1 | 17.7
8 | 0 | 433.4 | 464.1 | 62.3 | 13.5
8 | 1 | 494.5 | 493.6 | 64.7 | 18.7
32 | 0 | 1,150.2 | 1,138.6 | 212.9 | 13.1
32 | 1 | 1,449.2 | 1,239.6 | 237.1 | 18.1

Should save ~3% CPU in the trace on that issue, or 5 to 7 seconds.

Issues.Title: Add weekly CLI agent detection evidence audit
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Add a weekly and manually dispatched agentic workflow that inventories current CLI LLM detection rules, traces their signals through upstream harness source or vendor contracts, and researches up to five noteworthy missing harnesses.
- Independently inventory upstream identity signals for covered harnesses, tracing initialization, environment builders, hooks, and command launch. Report missing alternatives separately from the SDK inventory and new-harness candidates.
- Defer previous report narratives until fresh upstream research is complete, to avoid anchoring on old source paths and conclusions.
- Maintain one evidence-report issue, replacing its body on subsequent runs and stopping publication while the tracker is closed. Keep the audit report-only: no product changes, harness installation, runtime execution, or automatic pull requests.
- Add a separate, main-only manual fixer that accepts an audit run ID and one existing harness label. It can propose one additive presence-based alias and four generated regression cases through a draft PR. It never removes legacy signals, changes labels or matching policy, approves PRs, or merges them.
- Use the existing protected Copilot PAT pool, read-only agent permissions, restricted safe outputs, fail-closed threat detection, bounded research, and explicit incomplete-coverage reporting.
- Include generated workflow lock files, deterministic fixer guard tests, contributor documentation, and repository file-map entries.

## Audit validation

- Strict workflow compilation and schema validation passed.
- All 17 deterministic publication-guard cases passed, including absent output, malformed JSON, failure outcomes, missing/hidden markers, oversized reports, and duplicate terminal outputs.
- Native actionlint passed with only known gh-aw extension diagnostics excluded (`copilot-requests`, concurrency `queue`, and `github.aw`).
- Local Markdown links and heading anchors passed validation, including the updated workflow and contributor documentation.
- Initial hosted validation in a separate private repository verified report creation, replacement of the same tracker, preservation of its visible marker, and absence of duplicate trackers. The full audit covered all 25 labels and 41 SDK alternatives and evaluated five missing-harness candidates.
- A separate closed-tracker run emitted `noop`, preserved the report body exactly, and created no duplicate issue. The test tracker was reopened afterward.
- Two generic prompt revisions were evaluated through full hosted audits. The first still missed OpenCode's current signal. The second started with an answer-free tracker and independently discovered `OPENCODE=1`, tracing its bootstrap assignment through the inherited environment to command launch. Neither the missing variable nor its source path was supplied in the prompt. The model, tools, permissions, and research budgets were unchanged.

Initial hosted audit: https://github.com/baronfel/sdk-llm-detection-trial-20261028/actions/runs/40792986220

Closed-tracker check: https://github.com/baronfel/sdk-llm-detection-trial-20261028/actions/runs/40795210491

Successful blind investigation: https://github.com/baronfel/sdk-llm-detection-trial-20261028/actions/runs/40799598457

The validation repository is private, so those links require access. The trial substituted its own credential for the production PAT pool and pinned the SDK checkout to `7d24d6cf305b1d175811c32490bdd3d543ad51c1`. Production protected-environment authentication and installed harness runtime behavior were not exercised.

## Latest audit result

The blind trial report remained **Incomplete**: 6 signals Verified, 3 Mismatch, 1 False-positive risk, and 31 Unverifiable. All 41 SDK alternatives were represented. Missing evidence is not treated as proof that a detector is valid or should be removed.

The report identified `OPENCODE=1` as a missing alternative for the SDK's existing OpenCode rule, which checks `OPENCODE_AI`. The upstream bootstrap assignment is visible in [OpenCode's release source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/810c0eba1a7348036f8bdf61e6632d0c36c6876c/packages/opencode/src/index.ts#L64-L78). Finding a current signal does not prove that the legacy signal is absent from every supported path. Any product change still requires compatibility review.

Validation also exposed and fixed silent no-output success, proxy/source retrieval failures, workflow markers being stripped during issue updates, and shallow research anchored on earlier report citations.

## Manual fixer boundaries

- Require a successful main-branch audit run in this repository and its unique, open, bot-authored tracker. Recheck upstream stable-release evidence and block another proposal while a detection-fix PR is open.
- Generate and validate exactly one harness-prefixed alias in the existing presence rule plus four telemetry matrix rows. Preserve every other rule and existing test. Enforce two exact allowed paths, one AM commit, a 16 KiB patch limit, and rejection of bundles, mode changes, unrelated edits, or output-policy overrides.
- Select an immutable agent artifact ID from the current run attempt. A separate read-only validation job, without production secrets, a protected environment, or persisted checkout credentials, is configured to build the patched redist and run the existing telemetry detection matrix through `scripts/RunTests.cs`. Retain build/test diagnostics for seven days.
- Require successful isolated validation and threat detection before publication. Recheck the patch and PR metadata against the validated SHA-256 digest, check for duplicate PRs, and reject publication if `main` advanced. Only the separate restricted safe-output job can create the draft PR. No-op runs skip the build and PR-only checks.
- Structural restrictions do not prove upstream semantic claims. Source evidence, compatibility, and the proposed change still require human review. Rule removals, exact-value changes, new labels, and ambiguous signals remain outside this fixer.

## Fixer validation

- All **57 Node guard tests passed**, including real Git AM patch integration, legacy/test preservation, unrelated-code rejection, stale artifacts, incorrect audit provenance, unsafe inputs, mode/transport overrides, and acceptance/rejection through the publication digest CLI.
- Strict workflow compilation and schema validation passed. Native actionlint passed with known gh-aw extensions excluded and external shellcheck/pyflakes disabled.
- Compiled job-graph assertions verified read-only agent access, validation without protected secrets or write permissions, explicit publication ordering, an acyclic dependency graph, manual-only triggering, and serialized fix runs.
- All **197 local Markdown links and anchors** across nine documentation/memory files passed.

A hosted private fixer trial has now been dispatched for `opencode`, using audit run `40799598457` and the same pinned SDK revision. Publication is confined to the private trial repository, using its own credential. The adapter keeps exact snapshots of the relevant SDK files and performs validation in a separate complete SDK checkout after copying only the two structurally validated files.

The [first fixer run](https://github.com/baronfel/sdk-llm-detection-trial-20261028/actions/runs/40805282883) correctly stopped before agent activation when one Linux test fixture lost its deliberately staged executable-bit mutation during `git add`. The fixture now disables filesystem mode probing and explicitly asserts that the adversarial patch carries the intended mode change. The production restriction on executable files is unchanged.

The [retry](https://github.com/baronfel/sdk-llm-detection-trial-20261028/actions/runs/40805394346) has passed audit provenance and all guard checks and is proceeding through the hosted workflow. **Its SDK build, telemetry matrix, and draft-PR publication have not yet been established.** The earlier audit runs do not validate those fixer stages.

Issues.Title: Fix OpenCode environment detection
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Correct the SDK's OpenCode LLM environment marker from `OPENCODE_AI` to `OPENCODE`. Preserve the detector's existing presence-based semantics: any non-empty value identifies OpenCode.

Update the `dotnet test` output tests' environment-isolation list to clear the correct marker. Add regression cases for `OPENCODE=1`, another non-empty value, an empty value, and the incorrect `OPENCODE_AI` marker.

## Evidence

OpenCode's upstream shell tool explicitly sets `invocation.env.OPENCODE = "1"` before running commands:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/77a0fd6f3b247235b09941d55ff0faf72be1dae4/packages/core/src/tool/plugin/shell.ts#L214

The SDK previously checked `OPENCODE_AI`, so commands launched by OpenCode were not identified by that rule. With this fix, they receive the existing `opencode` classification and LLM-aware behavior.

## Validation

- Full Debug SDK/redist build completed successfully.
- Focused `dotnet.Tests` run through `scripts/RunTests.cs`, filtered to `CanDetectLLMStatusForEnvVars` and `GivenDotnetTestOutput`: **81 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Issues.Title: Archive VS transport component symbols directly through Arcade
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Archive symbols for SDK-built assemblies shipped in the Visual Studio template-locator and MSBuild-extensions transport packages through Arcade's existing loose-PDB publishing path, rather than relying on transport symbol packages.

- Enable `PublishWindowsPdb` for the .NET Framework builds of `Microsoft.DotNet.NativeWrapper`, `Microsoft.DotNet.SdkResolver`, `Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver`, and `Microsoft.DotNet.TemplateLocator` in official Windows builds only, excluding source-only builds.
- Disable `IncludeSymbols` on the two transport projects so they no longer generate `.symbols.nupkg` files. Regular transport-package contents are unchanged.
- Preserve the repository-wide Windows-PDB opt-out and existing `Microsoft.NET.Build.Extensions` task-symbol package coverage.
- Document the symbol-publication invariant in the Layout guidance.

Arcade converts/stages these PDBs in SymStore and collects them as loose PDB publishing assets. No custom uploader or symbol-server visibility change is introduced; existing feed configuration still controls visibility.

## Validation

- Passed 216 isolated MSBuild property-condition evaluations covering framework, OS, official-build, and source-only combinations, plus both transport symbol-package overrides (218 checks total).
- Parsed all six changed project files as XML, checked all seven local documentation links, and passed `git diff --check`.
- No local servicing build or test suite was run. The condition checks do not exercise compilation, PDB conversion, packaging, or upload.

Official Windows build validation is still required: confirm the four component PDBs are staged and listed as loose PDB assets, neither transport produces a symbol package, and symbol lookup succeeds after publication. PR validation alone may not exercise archival because it is gated on `OfficialBuild`.

Issues.Title: Simplify Hot reload browser tools availability check
Issues.Body:
Add build property `HotReloadBrowserToolsEnabled` that indicates that Browser Tools are enabled for Hot Reload.

Abstracts the implementation details of Browser Tools from the tooling. Previously a tool needed to track multiple properties and calculate the status of Browser Tools like so:

```C#
var enableHotReload = enableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile ?? string.Equals(configuration, "Debug", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

        if (!enableHotReload ||
            browserToolsAssetPrefix is not { Length: > 0 } ||
            !staticWebAssetsEnabled ||
            !jsModulesEnabled ||
            intermediateOutputDirectory is null)
        {
            return null;
        }
```

The PR moves this logic to the SDK targets.

Issues.Title: Make Visual Studio SDK selection conservative by default and honor global.json during compatible roll-forward
Issues.Body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Installing a newer .NET SDK can change which SDK an existing stable Visual Studio installation uses, even when the user has not explicitly opted into that change. We want stable VS and its associated SDK to behave as a coherent product by default, while preserving explicit ways to use newer SDKs.

There is a related resolver problem when `global.json` permits roll-forward: resolution can select an SDK that requires a newer MSBuild than the VS installation provides. Falling back to an arbitrary MSBuild-compatible SDK is not sufficient, because that SDK may violate the repository's requested version or roll-forward policy.

## Describe the solution you'd like

### 1. Default stable Visual Studio to its associated SDK

- [ ] With no `global.json` and no user opt-in to floating, use the SDK associated with the stable VS installation rather than automatically selecting a newer installed SDK.
- [ ] Keep an explicit opt-in path for users who want to float ahead of the SDK associated with VS.
- [ ] Preserve the repo-level override through `global.json`; do not treat the VS default as an unconditional cap on a repository's SDK choice.
- [ ] Cover VS-hosted builds and `MSBuild.exe` resolution, including command-line/CI use of VS MSBuild. This is not a proposal to apply the VS default to `dotnet build`.

The direction for Insiders/Canary VS is to float to newer compatible SDKs, including across feature bands, rather than adopting the stable and LTSC channels' conservative default.

### 2. Move and repurpose the VS preview-SDK option

- [ ] Replace the preview-only meaning of **Use previews of the .NET SDK** with an SDK-selection/roll-forward choice: stay with the SDK associated with VS, or allow floating ahead to a newer compatible SDK.
- [ ] Move the control out of **Preview Features**. The favored location is **Tools > Options > Projects and Solutions > SDK-style Projects**.
- [ ] Default floating off in stable/LTSC VS and on for Insiders/Canary.
- [ ] Coordinate the final location and presentation with the VS project-system team.

### 3. Refine compatible roll-forward in #53616 without ignoring customer intent

- [ ] When roll-forward chooses an SDK incompatible with the current VS/MSBuild, select an SDK that satisfies both the repository's SDK-selection constraints and the host's MSBuild requirements.
- [ ] Do not silently select an SDK below the version requested by `global.json`, or outside its allowed roll-forward policy, merely because it works with MSBuild.
- [ ] Preserve an error for an explicitly requested incompatible SDK rather than substituting an older one. If no candidate satisfies both sets of constraints, report a resolution/compatibility error.
- [ ] Add regression coverage for the case that the PR's current exact-match check misses.

Concrete example from the PR discussion: with `10.0.100`, `10.0.200`, and `10.0.300` installed, a `global.json` requesting `10.0.200` with roll-forward must not fall back to `10.0.100` when the selected newer SDK is incompatible with MSBuild. If no permitted SDK at or above the requested version is compatible, resolution should error.

The distinction is not simply whether the initially resolved SDK exactly equals the requested version. A different initial result does not authorize ignoring the original request.

### Scenario matrix / acceptance criteria

Build a shared truth table and resolver tests covering installed SDKs, VS channel/MSBuild version, the VS floating option, and `global.json` (`version`, `rollForward`, and `allowPrerelease`).

| Scenario | Intended outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Stable VS, no `global.json`, default setting, newer SDK installed | Use the SDK associated with VS. |
| Stable VS, no `global.json`, floating enabled | Float to a newer SDK compatible with the host and applicable preview-eligibility rules. |
| Insiders/Canary, no `global.json` | Float by default; include cross-feature-band cases. |
| `global.json` requests a compatible SDK | Respect the repository's SDK-selection policy rather than forcing the stable VS default. |
| Roll-forward's newest candidate is incompatible, but another permitted candidate is compatible | Resolve according to the policy among host-compatible candidates. |
| Explicit SDK request is incompatible, and only SDKs below the request work | Error; do not silently downgrade. |
| No SDK satisfies both repository constraints and host compatibility | Error with actionable diagnostics. |
| `dotnet build` | Do not introduce the VS-associated-SDK default into CLI SDK selection. |

Include restrictive and latest-style roll-forward policies, prerelease eligibility, exact requests, missing requested versions, and side-by-side VS installations. Remaining combinations need explicit expected results before implementation is considered complete.

## Additional context

**Scope and rollout**

- Do not retrofit the new selection behavior into VS 2022.
- This intentionally changes SDK selection for stable VS/MSBuild users without `global.json`. Installing a newer SDK alone would no longer opt those users into it; adoption may require the VS setting or repository configuration.
- The VS options work and SDK resolver work need coordinated tracking across their owning components.

**Open design details**

- Final option label, placement, and migration behavior for existing preview-option values.
- Complete precedence and prerelease-eligibility rules involving the VS option and `global.json`.

**Related work**

- #53616: Honor minimumMSBuildVersion when global.json rollforward resolves an incompatible SDK.
- [Reported fallback below the requested SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/53616#issuecomment-4145585895).
- [October 28 triage direction: satisfy both VS and global.json, otherwise error](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/53616#issuecomment-6477717493).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Make Visual Studio SDK selection conservative by default and honor global.json during compatible roll-forward" (#56817)

Issues.Title: Telemetry adds ~4s to a no-op dotnet build on .NET 11 RC2 (4.2s vs 0.14s with opt-out)
Issues.Body:
## Describe the bug

On SDK 11.0.100-rc.2, a no-op `dotnet build` takes about 4 seconds longer when telemetry is enabled. With `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` the same build takes 138ms.

I first noticed it in the Godot editor, whose "Build .NET project" step calls the CLI. MSBuild reported 0.09s, but the step took about 4s, even when nothing had changed.

The delay is nearly constant (4.19s to 4.21s over 10 runs), which looks like a fixed wait at shutdown rather than network latency.

## Steps to reproduce

```
dotnet new classlib -o lib
cd lib
dotnet build
hyperfine --warmup 2 --runs 10 -N 'env -u DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT dotnet build --no-restore -v q' 'env DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 dotnet build --no-restore -v q'
```

## Expected behavior

Telemetry adds no noticeable time to a command.

## Actual behavior

```
Benchmark 1: env -u DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT dotnet build --no-restore -v q (10 runs)
  Wall Time    4.197 s   ±   0.006 s      4.190 s   …   4.207 s
Benchmark 2: env DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 dotnet build --no-restore -v q (10 runs)
  Wall Time    0.138 s   ±   0.003 s      0.133 s   …   0.143 s
```

## Is this a regression?

Yes. The same test on SDK 10.0.401 (a `net10.0` copy of the project, pinned with `global.json`) shows no difference:

```
Benchmark 1: env -u DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT dotnet build --no-restore -v q (10 runs)
  Wall Time    422.3 ms  ±     7.4 ms
```

Issues.Title: File-based apps: strengthen ProjectRootElement cache
Issues.Body:
Fixes an issue discovered in equivalent code on the roslyn side: https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86235#discussion_r4399631291

Interleaved concurrent executions of the affected code path for the same virtual project could end up registering different ProjectRotElement instance in MSBuild vs our dictionary.

This shouldn't be currently reachable from normal `dotnet run` scenarios (we are not using the API concurrently like that, although that doesn't mean we shouldn't make it more resilient) but it seems that `dotnet watch` might be actually consuming these APIs in such a way that this could be hit.

Issues.Title: [aw] Detection Runs
Issues.Body:
This issue tracks all runs where threat detection flagged problems in agentic workflows in this repository. Each workflow run that completes with a detection warning or failure posts a comment here.

<details>
<summary>What is a Detection Problem?</summary>

A detection problem occurs when the threat detection system either:
- **Detects potential security threats** (prompt injection, secret leak, malicious patch)
- **Fails to produce results** (agent failure, parse error)

When `continue-on-error: true` (the default), these problems produce warnings and safe outputs still proceed. When `continue-on-error: false`, they block safe outputs entirely.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:
- Track workflows where threat detection raised concerns
- Review patterns of detection warnings or failures
- Identify false positives or recurring issues with threat detection
- Monitor the health of the threat detection system

</details>

- [GitHub Agentic Workflows Documentation](https://github.com/github/gh-aw)

Issues.Title: Add JSON output to dotnet sln list
Issues.Body:
`dotnet sln list` includes headers that prevent direct consumption by automation. This change adds machine-readable output without changing the default display.

- **Output formats**
  - Add `--format <table|json>`, defaulting to `table`.
  - JSON emits a sorted array of project paths, or `[]` for empty solutions.
  - Support solution filters and `--solution-folders`.

- **CLI integration**
  - Update help text and localization resources.
  - Use source-generated JSON serialization for Native AOT compatibility.

```sh
dotnet sln source.sln list --format json
# ["App/App.csproj","Lib/Lib.csproj"]
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #26303
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add JSON output to dotnet sln list" (#56808)

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.4xx] Distinguish Copilot CLI and VS Code agent detection
Issues.Body:
.NET 10 reports Copilot CLI as legacy `copilot` and misses VS Code agent signals. This backports the Copilot-specific detection changes without expanding unrelated detectors.

- **Detection**
  - Emit `copilot-cli` for upstream CLI signals.
  - Emit `copilot-vscode` for non-empty `COPILOT_AGENT` or `AI_AGENT=github_copilot_vscode_agent`.
  - Preserve `copilot-app` and multi-agent reporting; multiple signals for one client produce one label.

- **Behavior and compatibility**
  - Newly recognized environments inherit agent-friendly output: disabled MSBuild live-node display and MTP ANSI/progress output, independently of telemetry opt-out.
  - Document continued support for historical `copilot` labels; older data cannot reliably distinguish clients.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Cover individual signals, overlaps, empty/unrelated signals, no-agent environments, and MSBuild/MTP output effects.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #56745

Issues.Title: Installation of SDK v10.0.402 succeeds but does nothing when v10.0.403 is installed (by VS)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

We use a fixed version of the .NET SDK for some/most of our repos by using a global.json with **rollforward** set to "disabled".  Of course, we have a mechanism in place to update it for all repos :p

I recently installed version **18.11.2** of **Visual Studio 2026**, which comes with version **10.0.403** of the .NET SDK and which uninstalls version **10.0.402** of the .NET SDK.

I subsequently tried to reinstall version **10.0.402** of the .NET SDK using the standalone installer.
The installer completed almost immediately and reported success, but did not install version **10.0.402** of the SDK.
Is this by design? Until recently, installing an older SDK version worked fine.

Issues.Title: Print merged MTP code coverage summaries
Issues.Body:
Fixes #56796.

## Summary

- Negotiate counts-based MTP coverage summaries independently of the existing base protocol.
- Render `Code Coverage Summary` and invariant one-decimal percentages. A multi-application `Total` comes from a successfully accepted merged artifact, never from adding or averaging overlapping application measurements.
- Require complete input-path and execution/instance/session provenance before promoting a merged total. Preserve scoped measurements for incomplete, ambiguous, failed, or cancelled runs, including cancellation hidden by aggregate/ignore policies.
- Keep controller coverage arriving after session end, distinguish fallback source identities, and apply last-write-wins metric updates without combining producers.
- Add protocol, handler, provenance, lifecycle and rendering regressions; share renderer/serializer cases with the Native AOT test closure. Regenerate localized resources and document the CI line format.

## Dependencies and compatibility

The producer contract is introduced by [microsoft/testfx#12114](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/pull/12114). The coverage extension also needs its corresponding merged-artifact metadata update and an officially released MTP containing that API.

Those producer releases/dependency flow are required before rollout. The local candidate suffixes below are validation artifacts, not published dependencies, and are not added to SDK package manifests. Older peers keep their existing execution/artifact behavior without fabricated coverage. Coverage threshold evaluation and exit-code policy remain application-owned.

The existing supported base versions remain `1.0.0` through `1.3.0`; this does not enable the separate reverse-control protocol.

## Validation

- Full Debug redist build.
- Focused managed MTP/IPC/reporter suite: 272 passed, zero failed/skipped.
- Clean-published Native AOT coverage suite: 41 passed, zero failed/skipped.
- Real Windows x64 shipping-layout composition with genuine local packages:
  - MTP `2.6.0-preview.coverage-summary.20261027.1`.
  - CodeCoverage `18.13.0-preview.coverage-summary.20261027.2`.
  - Two applications each cover `6/12` lines of the same library; the actual merged Cobertura report and the printed total both report `12/12 = 100.0%`, not the per-application `50.0%`.
  - All 11 composed cases / 38 checks pass: single/multi-app, opt-out, no coverage, failure exit `2`, zero-result exit `8` with the actual `0/12` coverage, cancellation parity, originals retained, and managed/Native AOT `--test-modules` parity.
- Regression sensitivity: ten first-round, eight second-round, and six final-round assertions failed on the pre-fix behavior and pass with the fixes.
- Vendored-manifest, Markdown links/anchors, and diff checks pass.

Representative repository commands:

```powershell
.\build.cmd -c Debug
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CoverageSummary|FullyQualifiedName~FileArtifactMessagesSerializerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests|FullyQualifiedName~ArtifactPostProcessingManagerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationProtocolVersionTests|FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests"
.\test\dotnet-aot.Tests\run-aot-tests.ps1 -Trx -Filter "FullyQualifiedName~CoverageSummary"
```

The composed fixture uses two MTP applications referencing the same library and exercising complementary branches. With the built redist selected, representative commands are:

```powershell
dotnet test --solution CoverageFeature.slnx --no-build --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura --no-ansi --no-progress
dotnet test --solution CoverageFeature.slnx --no-build --no-artifact-post-processing --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura --no-ansi --no-progress
dotnet test --test-modules "**\bin\Debug\net11.0\Feature.*.Tests.dll" --no-ansi --no-progress -- --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura
```

This is main-branch Windows x64 evidence, not ARM64 execution or servicing/backport sign-off. Existing test-dependency audit/AOT rollup warnings were not suppressed. A separate development `dn` harness smoke encountered an SDK-directory assertion before module execution; the actual shipping-muxer Native AOT module checks above pass.

Issues.Title: Reconcile outstanding MTP vendoring updates
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Reconcile all four open `area-vendored-sync` reports against the verified upstream revision `3c6614c5ae19ee4ddca55cbf9b3375bbaad3496b`.

| Report | Reconciliation |
| --- | --- |
| #56696 | Port `AssemblyRunNotSelected` and wire it to successful affected-run orchestrators that never start a TestHost. Render a neutral `No affected tests selected` status without inventing skipped tests. |
| #56697 | Render successful zero-test runs with neutral `Zero tests ran` wording instead of a green `Passed!` verdict. Preserve real failures and the SDK's authoritative aggregate exit code. |
| #56698 | Retain the already-supported `AllowZeroTests` option, clarify its contract, and document why the SDK uses final aggregate exit codes instead of the upstream in-process `HasTestSessionFailure` callback and global `ZeroTestsPolicy` option. |
| #56786 | Mirror the comment-only clarification that GitHub Actions workflow commands use informational `DisplayMessage` forwarding verbatim. |

Update each reviewed source's exact commit/blob baseline and adaptation notes, regenerate all 13 CLI localization files through `UpdateXlf`, and document the SDK-specific reporting invariant.

## Compatibility

No wire IDs, advertised protocol versions, dependency versions, or feature gates change. The existing experimental affected-test gate remains in place. Mapping collection does not emit a no-selection status; rejected/partial handshakes, help/discovery, cancellation, and unsuccessful orchestrator exits cannot become benign no-selection results. Session failures, per-module policies, ignored exit codes, and failures in other modules retain their existing exit-code semantics.

This targets `main`; it does not enable a downstream feature or introduce a producer/consumer rollout requiring a servicing backport.

## Validation

Components: bootstrap SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102`, built SDK `12.0.100-dev` / `net12.0`, and the repository-aligned `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` package `2.6.0-preview.26519.1` (testfx revision `d25ab5d76da4d7202291e5d1af1070b5496751a9`). Confirmed that the deployed `dotnet.dll` matches the freshly built assembly before testing.

Successful managed layout build, exit **0**:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH = '0'
$env:DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT = '1'
& .\eng\build.ps1 /p:PublishAot=false /p:_ShouldPublishDotnetAot=false /m:1 /bl:artifacts\log\vendoring-layout.binlog /v:minimal
```

This machine lacks the MSVC/C++ prerequisites, so local verification disables native publishing. Native AOT publishing is not claimed; the changed command implementation is managed. Serial building also avoids concurrent managed/AOT projects writing the same XLF files.

Focused runner, exit **0**: **176 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.

```powershell
$filter = 'FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationActionQueueTests|FullyQualifiedName~RunAffectedTestsWithoutTestHost_ReportsSelectionAndSummary|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestSessionFailure_ShouldNotReportPassedSummary|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestProjectWithNoTests_ShouldReturnExitCodeZeroTests|FullyQualifiedName~RunNoTestsHonorsIgnoredExitCodeFromExplicitConfigurationFile|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestProjectWithTests_ShouldReturnExitCodeSuccess|FullyQualifiedName~RunMultipleTestProjectsWhereOneRanZeroTests_ShouldReturnExitCodeSuccess|FullyQualifiedName~RunAllSkippedTestsHonorsZeroTestsAndIgnoreExitCodePolicies'
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter $filter
```

The new composed-product tests use a real MTP execution orchestrator, its command-line registration, and the actual named-pipe transport—not mocked SDK handlers. They verify affected-run and mapping-collection success (host/parent exit `0`), nonzero orchestrator failures (`1`), a zero-test orchestrator exit without a TestHost (`8` becomes parent failure `1`), and framework session creation/closure failures (`10`). Existing cases cover ordinary successes, unexpected empty runs, strict/ignored zero-test policies, and mixed empty/passing modules. Unit cases retain legacy, partial/rejected handshake, discovery/help, and cancellation boundaries.

Additional successful checks:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe msbuild src\Cli\dotnet\dotnet.csproj /t:UpdateXlf /p:Configuration=Debug /p:TargetFramework=net12.0 /nologo /v:minimal /bl:artifacts\log\vendoring-update-xlf.binlog
python .github\scripts\check_vendored_files.py validate
git diff --check
```

Verified all four upstream blob identities, preserved source indexes and unrelated manifest entries, checked all generated localization entries, and resolved all local links in the changed guidance. Retained test artifacts: `artifacts\log\test-runs\dotnet.Tests\20261027-125533-81972\test-results.trx` and `build.binlog`; layout/localization binlogs are at the paths above.

Fixes #56696

Fixes #56698

Issues.Title: .NET October 2026 out-of-band security updates
Issues.Body:
On October 25, 2026, we released out-of-band security updates for .NET 8.0.33, .NET 9.0.22, .NET 10.0.14, and .NET 11 Release Candidate 3 (prerelease). We recommend updating affected applications and build environments as soon as possible. .NET Framework is not affected.

## Release Notes

* [Release details and feedback](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660)
* [.NET 8.0.33 and .NET SDK 8.0.133 / 8.0.427](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.33/8.0.33.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0))
* [.NET 9.0.22 and .NET SDK 9.0.123 / 9.0.320](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.22/9.0.22.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/9.0))
* [.NET 10.0.14 and .NET SDK 10.0.114 / 10.0.403](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.14/10.0.14.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0))
* [.NET 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 and .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 (prerelease)](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc3/11.0.0-rc.3.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0))

## Security advisories

| Advisory | Applicability | Announcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [CVE-2026-111497](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9) | Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write; all platforms when processing untrusted Brotli data. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/494) |
| [CVE-2026-114148](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-r6pf-x897-gm86) | Linux archive ownership; distribution-specific ASP.NET Core archives and source-build engineering inputs. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/495) |
| [CVE-2026-70197](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj) | Windows sockets memory corruption; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/493) |
| [CVE-2026-102870](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c) | Standalone Blazor WebAssembly debugger packages on .NET 10/11; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/492) |

The October 13 updates did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870. These out-of-band updates provide the corrected fixes; the original advisory identities and revision history are preserved. For CVE-2026-102870, update the affected standalone Server/DevServer package references; updating only the shared runtime is not a substitute.

For CVE-2026-114148, affected Microsoft-published .NET 8/9 ASP.NET Core runtime and targeting-pack tarball installations require a clean replacement following the advisory. Source-built archives are build/engineering inputs, not directly deployed production runtimes. Update those inputs and recreate their extracted workspaces using ownership-controlled extraction; review and rebuild affected downstream outputs as needed. .NET 10/11 applicability is limited to source-built distributions.

Also announced at [.NET October 2026 Out-of-Band Security Updates](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates/).

Please use the [release feedback issue](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660) for release-wide issues and the linked per-CVE discussions for advisory questions.
